newsitem.title: USA: Compaq Q2 exceeds consensus but not whisper. [CORRECTED 17:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Compaq Q2 exceeds consensus but not whisper. [CORRECTED 17:25 GMT]

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp's second quarter operating earnings surpassed the Wall Street consensus estimate of $1.39 but traders said the stock could trade lower because they did not meet the so-called "whisper" number.

Earlier Thursday, Compaq reported second quarter operating earnings of $1.48 a share, excluding a charge of $208 million or $0.73 a share for technology connected with its acquisition of Microcom. But the "whisper" number was about $1.50.
"Compaq is two cents light of the whisper number," one trader said. "Whisper" numbers refer to unpublished earnings estimates that circulate on Wall Street just ahead of earnings.

One analyst also said that Compaq's revenues of $5.0 billion were a bit light and that some were expecting revenues of about $5.1 billion. "It's a damn good number, but it's less than what is in the stock right now," said the analyst, who asked not to be named. Compaq's stock has surged almost $24 in the past 10 days ahead of earnings.

"The numbers roughly came in line; gross margins were a little higher," said David Wu, an analyst at ABN AMRO Chicago Corp. (Corrects company from ABN/Amro-First Chicago). "There is nothing really outstanding to note." Wu said that the consensus number of $1.39 on First Call was "a little low; no one believed those numbers."
"I don't think there is going to be any fireworks in the stock today," Wu added.

One technology trader said that Compaq's earnings, combined with comments by rival PC makers Hewlett-Packard Co and International Business Machines Corp that they will be aggressive in PC pricing along with Compaq, technology stocks will likely get hit Thursday. Compaq is expected to announce big PC price cuts later Thursday.
"Today is setting up for a bad day in the technology patch," the technology trader said.
